text:
john (ACME): Hey team — we removed user `u.jones@acme.com` from Okta group `acme-engineers` yesterday but they still show as `engineer` role in Redwood and can access a protected endpoint. SCIM logs show a DELETE for membership. Can someone help?
laura-cs: sorry about that, John. Can you paste the SCIM event id or the Okta group id? Also when was the removal approximately?
john (ACME): event id `evt_20260218_8342`, removal ~ 2026-02-18 17:12 PST. I can share a screenshot of the SCIM audit if helpful.
laura-cs: thanks — attaching the audit helped. I'm pinging @ashley-identity and @mike-eng to look at mapping + possible deprovision race.
ashley-identity: looking now. Quick checks: SCIM connector returned 200 on the push, but our provisioning worker logged a downstream 409 on role binding patch at 17:12:05. grabbing logs...
ashley-identity: log snippet:
```
2026-02-18T17:12:05Z provisioning-worker-3 ERROR applyRoleBindings user_id=u.jones@acme.com group_extid="okta:00ab12" result=conflict details="role_binding exists with external_id='okta:00ab12 '"
```
mike-eng: that trailing space on external_id looks suspicious — looks like Okta sent `externalId` with extra whitespace during an earlier group push. Our normalization trimmed on some code paths but not on delete path. That explains the DELETE not matching the existing role_binding row (mismatch on exact string).
laura-cs: so the user removal made a DELETE for `okta:00ab12` but DB had `okta:00ab12 ` (note space) so we left an orphaned role_binding.
sam-platform: reproducing locally — create group with externalId `okta:00ab12 ` (with space) then remove member with externalId `okta:00ab12` -> DB ends up with leftover binding. I'll run a quick fix.
mike-eng: short-term mitigation: script to trim external_id and re-run pending deprovisions for affected org. Longer-term: enforce normalized externalId on ingress and treat trailing/leading whitespace as equal in deprovision matcher.
ashley-identity: repro steps I'm saving for the ticket:
1) create Okta group with externalId including trailing whitespace
2) provision membership to user -> role_binding created with exact external_id
3) later Okta push sends deletion without trailing space -> provisioning engine calls delete by exact external_id and finds nothing -> binding remains

Command we used to force re-sync for John's org: 
```
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.example/v1/admin/orgs/42/scim/force-sync" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"okta_group_ids": ["00ab12"]}'
```
run it, it re-applied normalization and removed the orphaned binding.
laura-cs: patched John's account just now — John, can you confirm they no longer have access?
john (ACME): checked — access revoked. Thank you! Appreciate the quick turnaround.
ashley-identity: created internal ticket: PROV-7623. Plan: 1) backfill migration to trim external_id on all role_bindings (one-off db job), 2) add input normalization in provisioning worker, 3) add a fuzzy-match fallback on deprovision to catch whitespace and case differences for the next 30 days, 4) telemetry alert if deletions return no matches and the group had >0 prior members.
mike-eng: adding safe migration SQL snippet to ticket: 
```
UPDATE role_bindings
SET external_id = TRIM(external_id)
WHERE external_id <> TRIM(external_id);
```
We'll run this during the 02:00-03:00 UTC maintenance window and have a rollback plan.
sam-platform: also adding a one-off job to re-run deprovision for bindings where normalized external_id matched other members.
okta-bot: automated message — Okta push received for org=42 group=00ab12 at 2026-02-18T17:12:00Z status=200
laura-cs: John, I'll follow up via email with the incident summary and the ticket link. If anything else crops up in the next 24h ping me here and we'll expedite. Closing thread once migration completes. :+1:
john (ACME): perfect, thanks everyone.
laura-cs: closing notes: root cause = inconsistent external_id normalization between create vs delete SCIM paths; fix = normalize on ingress + backfill migration + temporary fuzzy-match fallback. Will monitor.
